question: Which calls involved a request for a security pack or SOC 2 documentation?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract every request by the prospect or customer for a security pack, SOC 2 report, SOC 2 documentation, security questionnaire, compliance certificate, penetration test results, or similar security/compliance documentation, including who asked, what was requested, and whether OrbitFlow staff agreed, deferred, or declined to provide it.
assumptions: No specific company or call type is named, so all calls in the catalogue are in scope.
'Security pack' and 'SOC 2 documentation' are treated as the core terms, with related security and compliance documentation included as synonyms.

findings.speaker: Tom Alvarez
findings.quote: we will ask for screenshots or documentation, not just yes/no answers on a questionnaire.
findings.context: Tom Alvarez requested the SOC 2 report, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, and retention documentation from OrbitFlow. — Customer request for security/compliance documentation; OrbitFlow staff agreed to provide it under the normal process.

findings.speaker: Tom Alvarez
findings.quote: Can you send the SOC 2 report, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation?
findings.context: Tom Alvarez asked for the SOC 2 report, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, and retention documentation. — Specific list of documents requested by the customer.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: Yes, all of that under the normal process, and we can complete your questionnaire.
findings.context: Maya Chen agreed to provide the security documents and to complete the customer's security questionnaire under the normal process. — OrbitFlow AE agreed; she also asked the customer to flag any absolute security gates early.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Baseline is SOC 2 Type II.
findings.context: Jon Bell stated OrbitFlow's security baseline: SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO and SCIM on Enterprise, encryption, audit logs, and EU residency on Enterprise. — Vendor staff describing security posture in response to the security review; not a document delivery.

findings.speaker: Tom Alvarez
findings.quote: We need the usual vendor review, SSO, audit logs. We don't have a special data-residency requirement for this project.
findings.context: Tom Alvarez said the security review list is short: usual vendor review, SSO, audit logs, and no special data-residency requirement. — Customer's stated security requirements for the project.

findings.speaker: Rachel Morgan
findings.quote: The gating issue isn't security for us.
findings.context: Rachel Morgan said security is not the gating issue; the real gate is whether the company expands its existing Workato contract. — Customer clarified the security review is not the blocker, contrary to Maya's invitation to flag gates.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: we document subprocessors.
findings.context: Jon Bell said LLM data handling questions from the customer's security team will be answered with documented subprocessors and enterprise API arrangements, and AI can be disabled or scoped out of the pilot. — Vendor response to anticipated security review of model usage; answer depends on configuration and provider.

findings.speaker: Elliot Greene
findings.quote: Add pen test summary.
findings.context: Elliot Greene asked for a penetration test summary to be added to the security pack. — Customer request for pen test documentation during the security-first portion of the call, after Maya listed the pack contents.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: What else can we send? SOC 2 report, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation — is that the pack?
findings.context: Maya Chen proposed the security pack contents (SOC 2 report, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation) and asked if that was the pack; Elliot confirmed with 'And yes' and added the pen test summary. — Vendor proposed the pack list; the customer accepted it and added pen test summary.

findings.speaker: Elliot Greene
findings.quote: And we'll send you our questionnaire, which is long, and I apologise in advance.
findings.context: Elliot Greene said BrightPath will send OrbitFlow its own security questionnaire, which he expects to be long. — Customer-side questionnaire that OrbitFlow is to answer; this is the customer sending a questionnaire to the vendor.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: They're all long. We'll complete it.
findings.context: Maya Chen agreed OrbitFlow will complete the customer's security questionnaire. — Vendor acceptance of the questionnaire despite its length.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: SOC 2 Type II is the baseline.
findings.context: Jon Bell stated OrbitFlow's SOC 2 Type II is the baseline certification; the report itself is to be included in the pack. — Vendor claim about its compliance posture, made in the baseline certifications discussion.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: We send the security pack — SOC 2, subprocessors, DPA, architecture diagram, retention docs, pen test summary.
findings.context: Maya Chen committed to sending the security pack, including SOC 2, subprocessors, DPA, architecture diagram, retention docs and pen test summary, as a next step. — Closing next steps of the call; the pack is an outgoing vendor commitment.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: I'll put it in the pack.
findings.context: Jon Bell deferred the specific retention floor to the document pack rather than answering on the call. — Customer asked for a retention floor; vendor declined to quote it verbally and pointed to the pack.

findings.speaker: Sophie Reed
findings.quote: We need a standard DPA.
findings.context: Sophie Reed requested a standard DPA (data processing agreement) from OrbitFlow. This is a privacy/legal document request, not a security pack or SOC 2 report, and no security pack or SOC 2 was requested in this call. — Raised during the security questions, alongside SSO and data processing location. No OrbitFlow response to the DPA request appears in the transcript.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: I'll also get you written answers on the Shopify trigger coverage and the default processing region.
findings.context: Leo Grant did not agree to provide a DPA and did not address the DPA request. He committed only to written answers on Shopify trigger coverage and the default processing region. — Leo's deferral covers data processing location, which Sophie raised as a security question, but not the DPA itself.

findings.speaker: Anika Bose
findings.quote: disaster recovery documentation, penetration test material
findings.context: Customer asked for disaster recovery documentation and penetration test material as part of governance review. — Listed among the headline governance items Anika Bose needs, to be sent formally later.

findings.speaker: Anika Bose
findings.quote: Disaster recovery documentation and pen test material — you have these?
findings.context: Customer asked whether OrbitFlow has disaster recovery documentation and pen test material. — Direct request during the architecture and governance section.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: Yes, both available under the normal security process, along with SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA, and an architecture diagram.
findings.context: OrbitFlow staff (Jon Bell) said DR documentation and pen test material are available under the normal security process, along with SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA, and architecture diagram. — Vendor agreed to provide these, gated by the standard security process.

findings.speaker: Anika Bose
findings.quote: Good. Send all of it. We will also send our questionnaire. It is two hundred and forty questions.
findings.context: Customer asked OrbitFlow to send the full security material and said DeltaWorks will send a 240-question security questionnaire. — Customer's request for all documentation plus a questionnaire to complete.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: We will complete it. If there are questions we can't answer we'll say "no" rather than "partially".
findings.context: OrbitFlow staff (Maya Chen) committed to completing the customer's security questionnaire and to answering unanswerable items with a plain 'no' rather than 'partially'. — Customer was skeptical ('Everyone says that'); vendor committed to a firm answer format.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: I'll send the security pack in parallel — SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation, DR documentation, pen test material.
findings.context: OrbitFlow staff (Maya Chen) committed to send the security pack in parallel with the follow-up, including SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention and DR documentation, and pen test material. — Recap of next steps at the end of the call; the pack is a vendor commitment with no date stated beyond 'in parallel'.

findings.speaker: Hannah Cole
findings.quote: The list is: SOC 2, SSO and SCIM, exportable audit history
findings.context: Hannah Cole listed SOC 2 as one of the auditability items she requires, as part of her security and compliance gate. — Customer request for SOC 2 among a list of auditability requirements; she framed these as gates that could kill the deal.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: SOC 2 Type II is the baseline.
findings.context: Nina Patel stated that SOC 2 Type II is the baseline OrbitFlow security attestation. — Vendor response to Hannah's SOC 2 requirement; she answered on the call and did not offer to send the report in this turn.

findings.speaker: Noah Williams
findings.quote: Assuming the security material lines up, I want to move.
findings.context: Noah Williams said he wants to move forward only if the security material lines up. — Conditional go-ahead on the security documentation, which is a gating item before sandbox and pilot.

findings.speaker: Noah Williams
findings.quote: Hannah's had the security pack for long enough to complain about it.
findings.context: Noah Williams referred to a security pack that Hannah Cole needs time to review before the pilot starts. — Customer timing dependency: the security pack must be delivered and reviewed before the sandbox and pilot begin.

findings.speaker: Hannah Cole
findings.quote: I'll need a week.
findings.context: Hannah Cole said she needs a week to review the security material. — Customer review time for the security pack, which sets the pilot start timing.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Then let's say the pack goes out tomorrow
findings.context: Leo Grant committed to send the security pack the next day, containing SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation, and encryption details. — Vendor agreement to deliver the security pack; it was agreed, with a timeline of the pack going out the next day and the sandbox by end of next week.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Security pack — SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation, encryption details.
findings.context: Leo Grant listed the security pack items OrbitFlow owes the customer, including SOC 2 documentation. — Vendor's written list of deliverables after the call, agreeing to provide the security pack and SOC 2.

findings.speaker: Samir Khan
findings.quote: Right, the rest of my list, so you have it. UK residency. Strict retention. Encryption. SSO and SCIM. Matter-aware access controls, which we've just discussed. Audit logs. An AI opt-out. Subprocessor disclosure. And confirmation that our content is not used to train shared models.
findings.context: Samir Khan listed the security and compliance items he needs OrbitFlow to cover, including subprocessor disclosure, audit logs, and encryption. — Customer's requirements list from the security review; it sets up the SOC 2 baseline answer and later the security pack request.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: SOC 2 Type II is the baseline.
findings.context: OrbitFlow states SOC 2 Type II is the baseline security attestation it offers. — Vendor answer to Samir's compliance list; a claim about the product's certification, not a document provided on the call.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: I'd send you the payload schema so your SIEM team can look at it before you commit to anything.
findings.context: Nina Patel offered to send the audit payload schema so Samir's SIEM team could review it before commitment. — Security documentation offered in response to Samir's audit export question.

findings.speaker: Samir Khan
findings.quote: Yes. Send that.
findings.context: Samir Khan accepted the offer and asked for the audit payload schema to be sent. — Customer request for security documentation, accepted by the vendor.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: We send the security pack — SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation, pen test summary.
findings.context: Leo Grant committed to sending a security pack including SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation, and pen test summary as a next step. — Next-steps summary at the end of the call; the pack is a vendor commitment, not yet delivered.

findings.speaker: Samir Khan
findings.quote: I'll want that confirmed in the pack rather than remembered from a call.
findings.context: Samir Khan asked that the AI-disable position be confirmed in the security pack, not left as a call statement. — Customer request that a security/compliance position be documented in writing; vendor agreed.

findings.speaker: Darren Wu
findings.quote: Some districts have their own questionnaire.
findings.context: Customer says some school districts have their own security questionnaire that Inkwell may need to pass; for larger districts, possibly, but not for a pilot. — Customer-side statement about district procurement requirements. Darren is the speaker; the 'possibly' hedge and 'not for a pilot' qualifier are his.

findings.speaker: Darren Wu
findings.quote: Possibly, for the larger ones. Not for a pilot.
findings.context: Darren says the larger districts may require OrbitFlow to complete their questionnaires, but not a pilot. — Response to Maya asking whether OrbitFlow would need to complete district questionnaires.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: I'd note that we should still complete your security review properly. Making the data question moot doesn't remove the vendor assessment.
findings.context: Vendor (Maya) says OrbitFlow should still complete Inkwell's security review properly, even though the data-boundary design makes the data question moot. — Vendor position on the security review, raised after the FERPA/student-data discussion.

findings.speaker: Olivia Grant
findings.quote: Maya, what do you owe us?
findings.context: Customer (Olivia) asks what OrbitFlow owes Inkwell after the call, which leads to a request for the security pack. — Olivia's question at the end of the call; the security pack request is part of the follow-up list she prompted.

findings.speaker: Maya Chen
findings.quote: The security pack — SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation.
findings.context: Maya commits to provide a security pack consisting of SOC 2 report, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram, and retention documentation. — Vendor agreement to deliver security documentation as a follow-up action in response to Olivia's request. The SOC 2 report is listed as part of the pack.

findings.speaker: Jon Bell
findings.quote: SOC 2 Type II baseline, SAML SSO and SCIM on Enterprise, encryption in transit and at rest, audit logs covering administrative and workflow events
findings.context: Jon (vendor) describes OrbitFlow's security baseline as SOC 2 Type II, with SAML SSO and SCIM on Enterprise, encryption, and audit logs. — Vendor's verbal description of its security posture in response to Darren's security list. This is a vendor claim, not a delivered report.

findings.speaker: Darren Wu
findings.quote: That's sufficient for us. We're not a bank.
findings.context: Darren says the vendor security baseline described is sufficient for Inkwell, so no further security documentation request was made at that point. — Customer reaction to the vendor's security list; it indicates the customer was satisfied with the verbal description on this call.

findings.speaker: Marcus Chen
findings.quote: Security list, Ava.
findings.context: Marcus Chen asked Ava to take over the security checklist review, which is the closest the call comes to a security review request. No security pack, SOC 2 report, or questionnaire was explicitly requested. — Prompt for a security review. Marcus names the list as the next item, but no document is requested by name.

findings.speaker: Ava Sinclair
findings.quote: Right. SSO and SCIM. Secrets management, which we've covered. Audit logs. Least-privilege credentials. Regional controls.
findings.context: Ava Sinclair listed the security requirements Juniper needs covered: SSO and SCIM, secrets management, audit logs, least-privilege credentials, regional controls, API limits, and workflow definition export. She asked for these to be addressed but did not ask for SOC 2 documentation or a security pack. — Security requirements list, not a documentation request. Some items were already covered earlier in the call.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: SOC 2 Type II is the baseline. SAML SSO and SCIM on Enterprise.
findings.context: Nina Patel said SOC 2 Type II is the baseline OrbitFlow offers, and described SSO/SCIM, encryption, audit logs, retention, and EU residency (Enterprise). She did not offer a SOC 2 report, security pack, or questionnaire. — Vendor's answer to the security list. It is a claim about the product's compliance posture, not a document offer.

findings.speaker: Grace Okonkwo
findings.quote: Which providers are on the allowed list currently?
findings.context: Grace Okonkwo asked which model providers are currently on the allowed list, a request for subprocessor information that falls under security/compliance review. OrbitFlow did not recite the list. — Part of AI-use due diligence, not a formal security pack, SOC 2 report, or questionnaire. Adjacent to the security/compliance documentation category.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: I'll send the current list with the subprocessor documentation rather than reciting it and getting one wrong.
findings.context: Nina Patel agreed to send the current allowed-provider list together with the subprocessor documentation, rather than reciting it on the call. — Deferred delivery. She chose to send the documentation to avoid getting a detail wrong on the call.

findings.speaker: Nina Patel
findings.quote: and the subprocessor documentation.
findings.context: The subprocessor documentation is one of four written answers OrbitFlow owes Halberd. Grace said she is supportive subject to these answers. — Listed as a condition of support for the AI rollout, with a due date of end of week.

draft.answer: Security pack or SOC 2 documentation was requested or committed in Acme Logistics, BrightPath Health, DeltaWorks Manufacturing, Ember Financial, Harbor Legal and Inkwell Learning [C1][C2][C3][C4][C5][C6]. Cedar & Finch asked only for a DPA, Juniper Cloud Tools requested no documents, and Halberd Security's request was for subprocessor documentation [C7][C8][C9].

claims.text: Acme Logistics (CALL-001): Tom Alvarez asked for the SOC 2 report, subprocessor list, DPA, architecture diagram and retention documentation; Maya Chen agreed under the normal process and offered to complete the questionnaire.

BrightPath Health (CALL-002): Maya Chen proposed the pack (SOC 2, subprocessors, DPA, architecture diagram, retention docs); Elliot Greene accepted and added a pen test summary; Maya committed to send it as a next step. BrightPath will also send its own questionnaire, which Maya agreed to complete.

DeltaWorks Manufacturing (CALL-004): Anika Bose asked for DR documentation and pen test material; Jon Bell said these are available with SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA and architecture diagram; Anika said 'Send all of it' and that DeltaWorks will send a 240-question questionnaire, which Maya Chen committed to complete. Maya later committed to send the pack in parallel with the follow-up, with no date beyond that.

Ember Financial (CALL-005): Hannah Cole listed SOC 2 among her gating requirements and Noah Williams made moving forward conditional on the security material; Hannah needs a week to review, and Leo Grant committed to send the pack (SOC 2, subprocessors, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation, encryption details) the next day.

Harbor Legal (CALL-008): Leo Grant committed to send a security pack including SOC 2 and a pen test summary; Samir Khan asked that the AI-disable position be confirmed in the pack, and accepted Nina Patel's offer to send the audit payload schema.

Inkwell Learning (CALL-009): in response to Olivia Grant asking what OrbitFlow owes them, Maya Chen committed to a security pack (SOC 2, subprocessors, DPA, architecture diagram, retention documentation). Darren Wu said the verbal baseline was sufficient and that district questionnaires are possible for larger districts but not for a pilot.
Cedar & Finch (CALL-003): Sophie Reed requested only a standard DPA, not a security pack or SOC 2; Leo Grant did not address the DPA request.

Juniper Cloud Tools (CALL-010): no security pack or SOC 2 report was requested; Ava Sinclair listed security requirements, and Nina Patel only stated SOC 2 Type II as the baseline. The finding that Marcus Chen handed over the security checklist is inferred.

Halberd Security (CALL-013, renewal): Grace Okonkwo asked which model providers are allowed; Nina Patel agreed to send the list with the subprocessor documentation, one of four written answers owed by end of week. This is not a SOC 2 or security pack request.
